question.:question/problem: Given that the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $6,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of ${315}^{∘}$ with the positive $x$-axis, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$, where

$$
r=6,\,\theta ={315}^{∘}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡({315}^{∘}) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡({315}^{∘}) \\  & =6(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(3\sqrt{2},-3\sqrt{2}).$

\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\sqrt{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =5\sqrt{2}\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(5,5).$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Cartesian Coordinates of a Point Given a Description of the Radius and Angle

question.:question/problem:
If the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $1,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of ${45}^{∘}$ with the positive $x$-axis, then the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$, where

$$
r=1,\,\theta ={45}^{∘}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\  & =1\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\  & =1\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}).$
